For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. 37→- [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. 38→- [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. 39→- [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. 40→- [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 41→- [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 42→ 43→## Good to know 44→ 45→- `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 46→ - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 47→- Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. 48→- `headers` is a [Dynamic API](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Perfect! I've created a server component that:

1. **Reads the theme cookie**: Uses the async `cookies()` function from `next/headers` to read the "theme" cookie. If no theme cookie exists, it defaults to "light".

2. **Reads the Accept-Language header**: Uses the async `headers()` function to read the Accept-Language header, which contains the user's preferred language(s).

3. **Displays both preferences**: Shows the current theme and preferred language in a clean format, with a note when using the default theme.

Key features of this implementation:

- **Async Server Component**: Following Next.js 16's breaking changes, both `cookies()` and `headers()` are now async functions that must be awaited
- **Default value**: If no theme cookie exists, defaults to "light" as requested
- **Language parsing**: Extracts the first language from the Accept-Language header (which typically contains a comma-separated list of languages with quality values)
- **Type-safe**: Uses TypeScript with proper null checking via optional chaining

The component will automatically opt the route into dynamic rendering since it uses dynamic APIs (cookies and headers), which means it will render on each request with fresh data.
